task: Diagnose why laptop cannot ping a PLC (10.12.0.86) and two Flex IO adapters (10.11.0.84, 10.11.0.89) on a TP-Link TL-SG605P unmanaged switch.

purpose: Read-only: confirm laptop Ethernet link and the secondary IPs configured on it
expected: Ethernet up with addresses in 10.11.0.x and 10.12.x subnets

output: Ethernet (Intel I226-LM) Up 100 Mbps; IPs 10.11.0.250/24, 10.12.0.250/16, 192.168.10.250/24 (manual). Three default gateways set on Ethernet (10.11.0.1, 10.12.0.1, 192.168.10.1). Wi-Fi also up (DHCP). Firewall on for all profiles.
deviation_notes: Noted: multiple default gateways on an isolated control network are unnecessary.

purpose: Read-only: verify routing goes out Ethernet and see whether devices answer ARP
expected: Routes on-link via Ethernet; if devices are present at those IPs, ARP resolves even if ICMP is blocked

output: Routes 10.11.0.0/24 and 10.12.0.0/16 on-link via Ethernet (correct). All pings time out. Neighbor entries for 10.11.0.84, 10.11.0.89, 10.12.0.86, gateways all Incomplete = no ARP reply from any device.
deviation_notes: No device answers ARP at its expected IP, so the problem is layer 1/2 or the devices are not actually at those IPs. Not a laptop routing or firewall issue.

command: Check admin elevation; Get-NetAdapterStatistics -Name Ethernet sampled over 15s
purpose: Planned a pktmon capture to see BOOTP/ARP from devices; check elevation first and measure live traffic

output: Not elevated (pktmon needs admin). Counter sample: 152 broadcast frames received in 15s, 0 unicast, 0 multicast.
deviation_notes: Could not capture packets without admin; fell back to counters. ~10 broadcasts/s arriving means devices are on the wire and talking, but not answering ARP for the expected IPs.
